title: Condo Loan Requirements in 2026: What Changed for Buyers
description: Fannie Mae changed its condo loan rules in 2026. What changed, why some condos can't get a regular mortgage, condotels, and your options if a building fails.
h1: Condo Loan Requirements: What Changed in 2026
dek: Fannie Mae changed its condo rules this year. Here's what it means if you're buying a condo.

faq.a: A non-warrantable condo is a unit in a building that doesn't meet Fannie Mae's rules, so it can't get a regular conventional loan sold to Fannie Mae. Common reasons are hotel-style operations, big unfunded repairs, one owner with too many units, or too much commercial space. It can still be financed with other loans.

faq.q: Did Fannie Mae get rid of Limited Review for condos?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae retired Limited Review for loan applications dated on or after August 3, 2026. Established buildings with more than 10 units now need a full review or FHA approval.

faq.q: Can I get a regular mortgage on a condo I rent out?
faq.a: Yes, if the building qualifies. Renting your own unit is fine. The building fails if it runs like a hotel, with a front desk, daily cleaning or a required rental program.
